short_original_excerpts.intro:
All Score and Choice answers from TypeSafe include a probabilities property representing the probability distribution across the options (for Choice) or levels (for Score). The shape of that distribution is what tells you how certain the model is: concentrated on one outcome means a confident answer, spread out means an uncertain one.
The answer’s confidence property collapses that shape into a single number from 0 to 1, so you can threshold on it without doing the math yourself. It is 1 when all the probability is on one outcome and 0 when the probability is spread evenly. (Noul answers don’t carry one; see Noul below.)
short_original_excerpts.How confidence is calculated / Noul: A Noul answer is a single probability ppp that the answer is yes, and TypeSafe returns no separate confidence for it. The probability already carries the uncertainty: a value near 0.5 is the model saying it is unsure, and the Noul page covers how to threshold on it directly.
short_original_excerpts.How confidence is calculated / Choice:
A Choice extends the same idea to any number of options. For a Choice with nnn options, where pmax⁡p_{\max}pmax​ is the probability of the selected option:
confidence=pmax⁡−1n1−1n\text{confidence} = \frac{p_{\max} - \frac{1}{n}}{1 - \frac{1}{n}}confidence=1−n1​pmax​−n1​​
This measures how far the top probability sits above an even split of 1n\frac{1}{n}n1​ per option, on a scale where the even split is 0 and certainty is 1. Only the top probability counts, so (0.6,0.3,0.1)(0.6, 0.3, 0.1)(0.6,0.3,0.1) and (0.6,0.2,0.2)(0.6, 0.2, 0.2)(0.6,0.2,0.2) both have confidence 0.4.








def choice_confidence(probabilities: list[float]) -> float:
    n = len(probabilities)
    return (max(probabilities) - 1 / n) / (1 - 1 / n)


choice_confidence(list(answer.probabilities.values()))
